what_happened: manager-microscope-20261003-1 ran git add -N on 11 new fixture files and then committed them through the commit tool in whole-path mode (004da816). The commit was right. But the shared .git/index kept the intent-to-add entries, and once HEAD moved they read as staged deletions of the 11 files just committed, so a plain git commit by anyone would have deleted them. The seat repaired it by hand with git reset -q -- <paths>. The tool moved a committed path's shared entry only when it equalled the old HEAD's, and an intent-to-add entry is neither that nor real staging. Fixed at 923ef407: the tool reads the intent-to-add bit and moves such entries to the new commit, saying add -N is not needed before it.
cue: an intent-to-add entry in the shared index survives a tool commit and reads as a staged deletion after the head moves
lesson: Keep the commit tool moving intent-to-add entries of committed paths to the new commit, with its fixture.
